answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each identity must solve a fresh random challenge whose input includes a public seed; solutions are logged as a ferrous ledger entry hash. Clones sharing one origin produce identical solution traces, so any duplicate trace across distinct IDs voids both. Honest agents diverge freely because their runtime state differs. An attacker cloning N identities must instead run N independent solvers, paying full compute and storage per clone—linear cost, no bulk discount. A basalt-anchored checkpoint stores the prior relic of each trace, making replay detectable.
